answer: Mass identity fraud is unattractive here not because it is always caught, but because it is never profitable to attempt at scale — the expected loss from slashing and rejection exceeds the expected gain. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a echo as the anchor of the cost.
